complexity.notes: Redundant: word_tuple is called twice per word; a single pass with d.setdefault(sig, []).append(word) (or defaultdict(list)) would be cleaner. The annotation tuple(int) is not valid typing (use tuple[int, ...]), and ord(letter)-97 silently assumes lowercase a-z input. `return list(d.values())` is more idiomatic than the final list comprehension.
complexity.space: O(n * L), for the output groups plus the dict storing all words and their 26-element signatures
complexity.summary: Each word is mapped to a 26-element letter-count tuple signature, and words sharing a signature are grouped together via a dict. The signature is computed twice per word: once to initialize dict keys and once to append each word to its group.
complexity.time_average: O(n * L), where n is the number of strings and L is the maximum string length
complexity.time_worst: O(n^2 + n * L), accounting for adversarial hash collisions degrading each dict lookup/insert to O(n)
